extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / broad public interested in wartime news and government policy
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item wartime newspaper page combining battlefield dispatches, international political news, and the full text and press coverage of President Roosevelt's executive order on wage and price stabilization. Includes reporting and quoted directives about price controls, wage freezes, and administrative powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceiling prices on commodities affecting cost of living
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of agricultural commodities the Price Administrator and the Administrator of Food Productions and Distribution (hereinafter referred to as the Food Administrator) are directed, and in the case of other commodities the Price Administrator is directed to take immediate steps to place ceiling prices on all commodities affecting the cost of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to agricultural and non‑agricultural commodities; immediate action is directed. (Source: President's executive order as printed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorize no further increases in ceiling prices except as legally required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of them is directed to authorize no further increases in ceiling prices except to the minimum extent required by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators must limit any upward adjustments to the legal minimum; presumes conservative use of authority to raise ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use discretionary powers to prevent profiteering and reduce excessive prices
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of them is further directed immediately to use all discretionary powers vested in them by law to prevent further price increases, direct or indirect, to prevent profiteering and to reduce prices which are excessively high, unfair or inequitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active use of all lawful discretionary authority is required to curb both direct and indirect price rises and to address inequitable pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted readjustments and supports for production without raising cost of living
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing herein ... shall be construed to prevent the Food Administrator and the Price Administrator, subject to the general policy directives of the economic stabilization director, from making such readjustments in price relationships appropriate for various commodities or classes, qualities or grades or from authorizing such support prices, subsidies or other inducements as may be authorized by law and deemed necessary to maintain or increase production, provided that such action does not increase the cost of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments, supports, subsidies and grade/class price readjustments are allowed when necessary to maintain/increase production, but only if they do not increase the overall cost of living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of agricultural Section 3 authorities to Food Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: The [functions] of Agriculture under Section 3 of the emergency price control act of 1942 ... are hereby transferred to, and shall be exercised by, the Food Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative authority related to Section 3 agricultural functions is explicitly reallocated to the Food Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on wage and salary increases (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The National War Labor Board, the Commissioner of Internal Revenue and other agencies ... are directed to authorize no further increase in wages or salaries except such as are clearly necessary to correct sub-standards of living, provided that nothing herein shall be construed to prevent such agencies from making such wage or salary readjustments as may be deemed appropriate ... to compensate ... for the rise in the cost of living between January 1, 1941, and May 1, 1942.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage/salary increases are broadly frozen except to remedy substandard living situations or to make specified cost‑of‑living compensations (the 'Little Steel' formula period referenced). Agencies retain limited discretion for rectifying substandard wages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted exceptions for promotions and merit adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor shall anything herein be construed to prevent such agencies ... from authorizing reasonable adjustments of wages and salaries in case of promotions, general increases, merit increases, incentive wages or the like, provided that such adjustments do not increase the level of pre-existing costs appreciably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable pay adjustments for promotions, merit, incentives, etc., are allowed so long as they do not appreciably raise overall pre-existing wage cost levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Manpower Commission hiring restrictions to prevent wage escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: The chairman of the War [Manpower] Commission is authorized to forbid the employment by any employer of any new employee or the acceptance of employment by a new employee except as authorized ... for the purpose of preventing such employment at a wage or salary higher than that received by such new employee in his last employment unless the change of employment would aid in the effective prosecution of the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New hires may be restricted to prevent upward pressure on wages; exceptions permitted where necessary for war‑effort effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct attention of public utilities and carrier rate authorities to stabilization program
rubrics_metrics.description: The attention of all agencies of the Federal Government, and of all State and municipal authorities, concerned with the rates of common carriers or other public utilities, is directed to the stabilization program ... so that rate increases will be per[mitted] and rate reductions effected, consistently with the act of October 2, 1942 ... in order to keep down the cost of living and effectuate the purposes of the stabilization program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities overseeing utility and carrier rates should align actions (rate increases or reductions) with stabilization goals and applicable law to control cost of living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of presidential stabilization powers to Economic Stabilization Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The Economic Stabilization Director is authorized to exercise all powers and duties conferred upon the President by that act, and ... is authorized and directed to take such action and to issue such directives under the authority of that act as he deems necessary to stabilize the national economy, to maintain and increase production and to aid in the effective prosecution of the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad discretionary authority is delegated to the Economic Stabilization Director to implement stabilization policy and issue directives under the cited statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of prior orders and regulations except insofar as inconsistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in so far as they are inconsistent with this order, Executive Order No. 9250 and the regulations issued pursuant thereto shall remain in full force and effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing stabilization orders/regulations remain operative unless they conflict with the new order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely dollar-and-cents ceilings on food commodities affecting living costs
rubrics_metrics.description: President Roosevelt said dollars-and-cents ceiling prices probably would be placed on all food commodities which affect living costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy intent communicated: specific numeric ceilings (dollars-and-cents) expected for foods important to cost of living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of price ceilings at retail level (default)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Byrnes said the food prices would be applied at the retail level rather than at the farm, unless some law requiring fair margins makes it necessary to fix prices back of the retail level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default implementation is retail-level ceilings; upstream (farm/wholesale) ceilings only if legally necessary to ensure fair margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of regional/area price handling
rubrics_metrics.description: He indicated ... that the question of determining specific food prices might be handled regionally, or by areas, so as to avoid a situation such as developed recently in Washington.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators may set prices by region/area to reflect local supply/scarcity and avoid abrupt swings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roll-back of certain market prices with producer support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government intends shortly ... to roll back the market price of live hogs from current levels ... and at the same time provide 'support prices' to give hog producers additional payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of policy mix: lower consumer prices combined with producer supports to stabilize farm income while reducing retail costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of ceiling prices in stores and advertising to enable consumer policing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the plan the OPA is working on, ... it will be possible for the purchaser to see the ceiling price in the store on the article he wants to buy and the prices will appear in advertising. The housewives, he said, will have to do the police work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPA planned visible labeling of ceiling prices at point of sale and in advertising, relying on consumers to help enforce price ceilings by recognizing overcharges.
